summary.text: Helena Scott is a Democratic member of the Michigan House of Representatives for the 8th District, which covers northwest Detroit, Ferndale and Pleasant Ridge.
Her House Democrats biography describes her as a former organizer and longtime labor and social justice activist, and lists her as minority vice chair of the Communications and Technology committee.

paragraphs.text: Scott graduated from Marygrove College with a bachelor's degree in psychology and political science, according to her biography.

Before joining the Legislature she worked in the airline industry for more than 20 years as a sales and service instructor, and she worked as community liaison for her predecessor, former Rep. LaTanya Garrett.

As lead organizer for Southeast Michigan Jobs with Justice, Scott led a petition drive gathering more than 5,000 signatures for the One Fair Wage ballot initiative, and she later served on the steering committee to protect and defend One Fair Wage.

The biography says she formerly served on the executive board of the Coalition of Labor Union Women and the Detroit League of Women Voters and was vice chair of the Michigan Democratic Party Black Caucus.
It says she chairs the bicameral Legislative Care Caucus, is historian of the Michigan Legislative Black Caucus and serves on the board of Detroit Horse Power.
Her committees are listed as Communications and Technology, Judiciary, and Natural Resources and Tourism.
The biography says she has two young adult children, Rick and Samantha Scott.
